turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Morning, Nate. Quick heads-up — I migrated the customer schema last night.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Oh, you did? I thought we were waiting until Friday. Did you take a backup first?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I took a full snapshot before the migration, so we're covered. I didn't bother with a separate backup — the snapshot should be enough.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hmm, snapshots are fine, but they're not the same as a proper backup. Anyway, how did it go?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Mostly fine, but I noticed a few customer records look off — some addresses got scrambled. I think the migration script had a bug.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Scrambled? That's bad. Can we roll back?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: The migration could always be rolled back — I made sure of that. But the corruption seems to have spread to the backups too. It's going to take days to repair.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Days? That's a nightmare. I told you we should have had a proper backup strategy.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I know. I'm setting up point-in-time recovery snapshots now, independent of the regular backup. That way we can restore to any moment.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. Let's hope that's enough.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey, Melanie. I heard the corruption repair is done. How's the data looking?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Clean now. But I have to admit, I deployed a new feature yesterday without running the test suite — I was in a rush.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: You what? After last week's mess, you're deploying untested code?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I know, I know. And of course, a regression slipped into production — the login flow is broken for some users.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Unbelievable. We need to fix this immediately, and we need a process to prevent it.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Agreed. I've set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests. From now on, untested code never reaches production.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That's a start. But what about the current regression? Can you roll back?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yes, the migration rollback still works, and I have the point-in-time snapshots. I'll revert the deploy and then push the fix with tests.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Alright. Let's hope the CI gate holds.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning, Melanie. How's the new CI gate working out?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: It's working — no untested code has reached production since. But I've been thinking about the snapshot issue.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: The snapshot you took before the migration? I thought that was fine.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Turns out that wasn't enough. The snapshot was taken hours before the deploy, and by the time we actually ran the migration, the data had changed. The snapshot was already stale.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: So what did you do?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I was wrong about relying on a single snapshot. We replaced it with continuous replication — we now stream every change to a separate system in real time. Snapshots went stale by deploy time, but continuous replication gives us a live copy.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That makes sense. So if something goes wrong now, you can restore to the exact moment before the bad change?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Exactly. And with the CI gate, we shouldn't have bad changes in the first place. But if we do, we can roll back to any second.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. That's a solid setup. Let's hope we don't need it.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Fingers crossed. But at least now we're prepared.
